primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators III: Pseudo-Differential Operators
primary_antecedent.edition: Springer 2007, reprint of the corrected 1994 edition
primary_antecedent.locator: Sections 18.3 and 24.7; Propositions 24.7.1 and 24.7.1-prime, printed pages 465–467, state the admissible-source and Banach observation framework.
primary_antecedent.receiving_contribution: Independent full-kernel construction of finitely many admissible source tests controlling an ordinary H2 regularization, its equation and traces, with a precise parameter-dependent scope.

source_correspondence: R0 uses one actual Banach-controlled negative Sobolev order. It states compact smooth finite-matrix coefficients, bounded full-kernel families, the precise negative regularizer order and uniform full microsupport hypotheses.

R1 retains the x-inverse ordinary kernel and the dy=x dt Jacobian. Theta and its inverse multiply the entire ratio kernel by t and t-inverse. Delta differentiates at fixed ratio. In compact resolved coordinates only finite side-face poles arise, absorbed by all-derivative flatness.

R2 proves the complete normal identities, including the input normal derivative, and the exact automorphism and twisted Leibniz rules. The inverse is a kernel operation. No residual term or lower-order generator term is discarded.

R3 proves D_x squared A u = Theta squared A f + D_x V u + W u, retaining ordered matrix coefficients, actual compact supports and orders m+1 and m+2. Moving the normal derivative outside V avoids assuming normal regularity of the input.
R4 proves the exact tangential quotient norm identity using the common one-sided isometry. Two intrinsic normal steps then give the ordinary one-order gain; no arbitrary extension is differentiated.

R5 constructs a finite recursive source list. The base is the actual order-zero bound on the Banach-controlled negative Sobolev space. Every child has the required order; every source target is nonpositive through precisely N+2 gains.

R6 proves the exact list-length recurrence, maximal source order minus two, fixed compact supports and uniform off-cone symbol estimates. An elliptic negative-order regularizer is realized with its full residual remainder. Its estimate is not silently inverted into an unregularized estimate.
R7 obtains ordinary H2, the L2 equation of the regularized vector and both actual Sobolev traces. The complete boundary kernel preserves zero Dirichlet values on smooth inputs.

R8 identifies the tested-graph completion inside B. Interior output tests transpose to compact input tests flat at the boundary; the source pairing is therefore continuous under B convergence. L2 uniqueness identifies each source component and actual Au, with convergence of both traces. No graph density is inferred from Banach density.

R9 controls each fixed tangential or b derivative word applied to a residual regularizer, with its own finite residual source tests. It distinguishes two normal derivatives from arbitrary ordinary smoothing and leaves parameter-independent tester reduction and the full observation theorem active.

Three complete solutions count the 21 source nodes for N=1,d=1, compute the full shifted quadratic generator including its constant term, and give a compact residual kernel with bounded source norm but unbounded third normal derivative.

The exact figure shows 1,4,16 source nodes at maximal orders minus 6,minus 4,minus 2 and the normal recovery/source indices. All labels, nodes, arrows and the complete desktop and sampled mobile reader were inspected.
Twenty-seven exact checks, 227 parsed formulas, 26 displays and thirteen inspected captures assist this review. They do not replace the full kernel, quotient-space or graph-completion proofs.
